analysis:
Examined the two head_text excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 1254-1648). The file is documentation only. The changed ranges are a large expansion of the changelog from line 6 onward, and the supplied patch excerpt is truncated. No executable code, configuration, authorization logic, cryptography or wire-protocol change is visible in these units.

The prose records security-relevant behavior but changes none. It covers the cache-routing persistence write-behind (no prompts, raw chain hashes or memory-tier holders persisted), the SSD prefix-cache write budget raised from 150 to 750 GB/day, the TTL moving from 15 to 30 minutes with the SEC-035 re-acceptance, the removal of the unauthenticated earnings endpoint (T-031), App Attest rotation and recovery limits, and the fail-closed attestation challenges.

Relation to the threat model: the T-041 text for the SSD cache already states a 30-minute TTL and HMAC-keyed lookup, which matches the changelog. The changelog mentions a raised daily SSD write budget. That affects disk wear and availability but not confidentiality, and the T-041 definition does not tie a specific write budget to a mitigation. The changelog describes cache-routing persistence on the coordinator, which is backend-owned and outside this provider-scoped model. Whether the persisted holder state weakens cross-account scoping cannot be determined from changelog prose.

No finding is raised. The actual implementation behind these entries (SSD cache budget, persistence, App Attest rotation) is not in the supplied evidence. Any claims there need review against the source in the code-bearing units of this PR, which this pass did not see.
